_meta.description: Translator-context sidecar for auth.invite. Workspace-invite entry surface and the invite-create surface.
_meta.audience: Users who have an invite link or code from a workspace owner (entry surface) and workspace owners creating an invite (create surface).
_meta.tone: Welcoming for the entry surface; clear and corrective for the create surface error messages.

form.fieldPlaceholder: Placeholder shown inside the Input when empty.
form.hint: Helper text rendered under the field, explaining what happens after submit.

errors._use: Client-side validation messages for the invite token field.
errors.empty: Shown when the field is submitted empty.
errors.invalid: Shown when the value does not match the invite-token shape.
errors.length: Shown when the value is outside the allowed length range. The fixed numbers reflect the gateway contract; do not translate them as words.

create._use: BUG-AUTH-8: Backend-driven error messages surfaced inside CreateInviteForm when the accounts-service rejects the request with a closed-set code. MAIL-6 (2026-06-03): adds success-state copy reflecting that the backend now actually dispatches the invitation by email.

success._use: Rendered after the accounts-service accepts the invite create AND the gateway returns a 200. Copy reflects MAIL-5 dispatch — the backend mailer fires after the row insert. The Copy-link affordance is preserved alongside the email for the 'didn't arrive' fallback.
success.title: Title of the success Alert. Keep short.
success.body: Body of the success Alert. ICU placeholders: {email} is the invitee address (already lowercased + trimmed by the form); {expiresAt} is a pre-formatted locale-aware date string from the form. Do not split the placeholders across sentences.
success.copyLinkSecondary: Helper text shown next to the Copy-link button after success. Acknowledges that the email may not arrive (spam, deliverability) without alarming the user.

errors.selfInvite: Shown when the workspace owner submits their own email address. Backend code: SELF_INVITE (HTTP 400). Keep the copy short and corrective; do not lecture the user.
errors.alreadyMember: Shown when the invited address already has an active membership in this workspace. Backend code: ALREADY_MEMBER (HTTP 400). Do not name the existing member; the UI only surfaces the rejection.

resend._use: MAIL-6 (2026-06-03): copy for the post-create Resend affordance. The accounts.invites.resend handler ROTATES the invite token on every resend (success AND failure) — the previous emailed link dies regardless. The UI must communicate this clearly so the operator does not accidentally invalidate a working link they were about to share manually.
resend.button: Primary CTA label for the Resend button. Keep short.
resend.buttonSending: Label rendered while the resend request is in-flight. Use a present-continuous form.
resend.success: Inline alert shown after a successful resend. The 'previous link has been invalidated' clause is REQUIRED — it tells the operator that any copied link they had open is now dead.
resend.confirmHint: Helper text shown BELOW the resend button BEFORE click. Mirrors the post-resend success copy so the operator can decide to resend or to copy the existing link first.

errors._use: Closed-set MailerError / DomainError code → localized copy. Hostile / unknown codes fall back to 'generic'. NEVER echo provider error text — keys map by code only.
errors.rateLimited: Backend code: RATE_LIMITED (HTTP 429). Triggered when email_attempts >= MAIL_RESEND_MAX_ATTEMPTS (default 5).
errors.notPending: Backend code: INVALID_STATE (HTTP 409). The invite has been accepted, cancelled, or expired since creation.
errors.expired: Backend code: GONE (HTTP 410). The invite's expires_at has passed.
errors.notFound: Backend code: NOT_FOUND (HTTP 404). Either truly missing OR a cross-workspace probe — both surface the same envelope (no enumeration oracle).
errors.forbidden: Backend codes: FORBIDDEN / FORBIDDEN_ACTOR_KIND (HTTP 403). Authz denial OR an api_key actor tried to resend.
errors.generic: Fallback for unknown closed-set codes and unexpected failures (network, timeout, 5xx). Defense in depth.
